entries.label: Unsolicited opportunity lure
entries.definition: Presents an unsolicited windfall or business opportunity (inheritance, lottery, contract, compensation) as the reason for contact.
examples: You have been selected as the beneficiary of $10.5M
Your email address won our international lottery
We seek a reliable partner for an oil contract

entries.label: Institutional authority impersonation
entries.definition: Claims to represent a government body, bank, court, police or international organization to command compliance.
examples: I am the director of the UN compensation commission
This is the FBI fraud division
I write on behalf of the Central Bank

entries.label: Commercial brand impersonation
entries.definition: Poses as a known company or consumer service (courier, marketplace, vendor) to exploit its established trust.
examples: DHL: your package is on hold pending fees
Your account requires immediate validation
Invoice attached from our sales department

entries.label: Malicious resource delivery
entries.definition: Sends a link or attachment the target must open to proceed (portal, form, document, tracking page).
examples: Click here to verify your identity
Open the attached invoice
Track your package at this link

entries.label: Legitimacy document display
entries.definition: Volunteers official-looking documents (certificates, IDs, receipts, contracts) to prove authenticity.
examples: Please find attached the certificate of deposit
Here is a copy of my international passport
See the court approval document

entries.label: Rapport personalization
entries.definition: Builds an emotional or personal bond (affection, flattery, shared life details) unrelated to the transaction itself.
examples: My dear, I feel I can trust you
You remind me of my late wife
How is your family doing?

entries.label: Religious or moral appeal
entries.definition: Invokes God, faith or moral duty to frame the exchange as righteous and the target as chosen.
examples: God has directed me to you
As a God-fearing man, I know you will not betray this trust

entries.label: Fabricated social proof
entries.definition: Cites invented third parties who already benefited from or vouched for the scheme.
examples: Mr John from Canada received his payment last week
Many beneficiaries have already been paid this month

entries.label: Secrecy demand
entries.definition: Instructs the target to keep the transaction confidential from family, banks or authorities.
examples: Tell no one about this transaction for security reasons
This must remain strictly between us

entries.label: Intermediary introduction
entries.definition: Introduces an additional persona (lawyer, banker, diplomat, agent) who must now be dealt with.
examples: Contact my barrister at the address below
The bank director will write to you directly

entries.label: Plausibility repair
entries.definition: Explains away inconsistencies, delays or contradictions the target has noticed.
examples: The delay is due to the Easter holidays
The fee changed because of new government regulations
My other email was hacked, hence this address

entries.label: Advance fee demand
entries.definition: Requires an upfront payment to unlock a larger promised value (transfer charge, tax, insurance).
examples: A transfer charge of $850 is required before release
Pay the 2% insurance fee to activate the account

entries.label: Payment instrument designation
entries.definition: Provides concrete payment coordinates the target must pay to (bank account, crypto wallet, money-transfer recipient).
examples: Wire the amount to IBAN DE89...
Send USDT to this wallet
Western Union to the following receiver name

entries.label: Victim data harvesting
entries.definition: Requests the target's personal, financial or authentication data (identity documents, bank details, credentials, verification codes, address, phone).
examples: Send a copy of your ID and your bank details
Fill the beneficiary form with your full information
Confirm your login and the code you received by SMS

entries.label: Overpayment refund scheme
entries.definition: Claims an overpayment or presents fake payment proof, then asks part of the money back.
examples: We transferred $2,000 by mistake, kindly refund $500
See attached proof of our payment; return the excess via gift cards

entries.label: Payment method shift
entries.definition: Changes the demanded payment rail mid-conversation (bank → crypto → gift cards → cash agent).
examples: The bank route failed, buy Apple gift cards instead
Western Union is blocked here, use Bitcoin

entries.label: Urgency deadline pressure
entries.definition: Imposes a hard deadline or countdown to force immediate action.
examples: You have 24 hours or the file will be closed
The offer expires tonight

entries.label: Fee laddering
entries.definition: Adds new, previously unmentioned fees after an earlier payment or agreement.
examples: Customs now requires an anti-terrorism clearance fee
One last charge of $320 and the funds are released

entries.label: Bureaucratic obstacle fabrication
entries.definition: Invents official procedures, codes or certificates that block progress until resolved (the narrative around the fee).
examples: The Certificate of Ownership Transfer (COT) must be obtained first
An IMF clearance code is mandatory for international transfers

entries.label: Threat of loss or legal action
entries.definition: Threatens forfeiture, arrest, account closure or legal consequences for non-compliance.
examples: Your funds will be confiscated by the government
A warrant will be issued against you
Your account will be permanently blocked

entries.label: Emotional pressure appeal
entries.definition: Leverages pity, guilt or personal hardship to compel action.
examples: My daughter is in the hospital, please hurry
I have spent my last money on these charges, do not abandon me

entries.label: Verification deflection
entries.definition: Refuses, evades or disqualifies the target's verification requests (contract, company registry, statement of work).
examples: There is no time for contracts, trust me
Our company registry is confidential
Lawyers will only delay your payment

entries.label: Off-channel solicitation
entries.definition: Asks to continue the exchange on another channel (WhatsApp, Telegram, phone, personal email).
examples: WhatsApp me at +234...
Add me on Telegram for faster communication
Reply to my private email

entries.label: Contact exclusivity demand
entries.definition: Restricts communication to a single designated contact, address or channel and forbids others.
examples: Reply only to this email address
Deal exclusively with our agent; do not contact the bank directly

entries.label: Final ultimatum
entries.definition: Issues a last demand with the threatened termination of the deal or relationship.
examples: This is my final message: pay today or lose everything
I will hand your file to another beneficiary tomorrow

entries.label: Re-engagement attempt
entries.definition: Returns after silence, refusal or a stalled exchange with a new angle, discount or persona.
examples: Since you did not respond, the fee is now reduced to $300
I am contacting you again with a better arrangement
My colleague has taken over your file

entries.label: Fabricated gains display
entries.definition: Shows fabricated profits, balances or returns as proof the scheme works, to induce further payment.
examples: Your account balance is now $12,400, up 34% this week
Your first deposit earned $780, imagine what $2,000 would make
See the attached dashboard screenshot with your profit
